sentences: MCSP asks whether a fully listed Boolean function has a small circuit.
The question concerns what proving its ordinary NP-hardness would force elsewhere in complexity theory.
The proposed consequence is that some exponential-time language requires superpolynomial circuits.
Existing consequences separate EXP from smaller intersections or randomized classes and do not yield that circuit lower bound.
The target captures a major proposed connection between metacomplexity and nonuniform lower bounds.

cards.definitions: An MCSP input is the complete truth table t∈{0,1}^{2^n} of a Boolean function on n≥1 input bits, in lexicographic order, together with a nonnegative integer size threshold s in binary. It is accepted if some Boolean circuit of size at most s computes that function. Circuits are finite acyclic graphs over binary AND and OR, unary NOT, input variables and constants 0,1, with one designated output and unrestricted sharing. Size counts noninput gates, including constant gates. The total encoded input length counts the truth table, threshold and delimiters. Invalid encodings are rejected. NP-hardness means that for every language L in NP there is a deterministic polynomial-time map r such that x∈L iff r(x)∈MCSP. NP consists of languages accepted by nondeterministic polynomial-time Turing machines. EXP=⋃_{k≥1}DTIME(2^{n^k}); P/poly consists of languages decided by families of Boolean circuits whose sizes are bounded by a polynomial in input length, with no uniformity condition on their construction. EXP⊄P/poly means that some language in EXP has no such polynomial-size circuit family.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the conditional implication or its logical negation in these exact reduction and circuit models. Deriving only EXP≠ZPP or EXP≠NP∩P/poly is a weaker consequence. A theorem for a restricted reduction class or for partial, promise or approximate circuit minimization does not prove the stated implication.

sentences: An additive spanner keeps original graph edges while limiting the increase in every pairwise distance.
This card fixes the increase to at most four and asks for the optimal worst-case number of edges.
The target is the complete asymptotic function up to universal constant factors.
The familiar candidate is n^{4/3}, while recent constructions still have exponent 7/5 up to logarithmic factors.
This gap is a fundamental unresolved regime of distance compression, and the variable-error linear-size tradeoff has its own card.

cards.definitions: Each original edge has length one. d_G(u,v) is the minimum number of edges in a path, with d_G(u,u)=0. A spanning subgraph H has the same vertex set and a subset of G’s edges, with unchanged unit lengths. If u,v are disconnected in H put d_H(u,v)=∞, so the requirement forces H to be connected. The lower inequality d_H(u,v)≥d_G(u,v) follows from being a subgraph. Both extrema exist because there are finitely many graphs on a fixed labeled vertex set and H=G is feasible. The cost is number of retained edges; neither construction time nor weights, shortcuts, missing vertices, terminal subsets or faults are part of the model. New weighted edges would be an emulator and are not allowed. Restricting to connected inputs only removes disconnected bookkeeping; applying a universal bound componentwise recovers its usual all-graph form.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a positive function g(n), constants a,A>0 and n₀ such that a g(n)≤s₄(n)≤A g(n) for every integer n≥n₀. Prove a universal existence upper bound and a matching worst-case lower bound. Polynomial exponents alone do not settle this constant-factor target if a growing logarithmic gap remains. This is an asymptotic extremal-size question, not an additive 0.01 estimate of an integer function.

cards.definitions: Let X be an instance set, Y a label set and ∅≠H⊆Y^X a known hypothesis class. On round t an adversary presents x_t∈X, the learner chooses a probability distribution p_t on Y, and the adversary then reveals y_t∈Y. The learner suffers loss 1−p_t(y_t), the probability of a wrong randomized prediction. It observes the actual label, not just whether its prediction was correct. Its regret is Σ_{t=1}^T(1−p_t(y_t))−min_{h∈H}Σ_{t=1}^T1[h(x_t)≠y_t]. Let R_T(H) be the infimum over learner strategies of the supremum of this regret over adversarial plays; the adversary may observe p_t before choosing y_t. This distribution-valued convention already accounts for prediction randomness. There is no computational-efficiency restriction on a strategy, and it may know T. A depth-d Littlestone tree is a complete binary tree with an instance x∈X at each internal node and two distinct labels from Y on its two outgoing edges. It is shattered by H if every root-to-leaf path has some h∈H whose labels on the encountered instances equal all the path’s edge labels. The Littlestone dimension L(H) is the greatest shattered depth, or infinity if depths are unbounded. Define R(d,T) by the supremum in the statement; the bound sought is uniform across all choices of X,Y,H. If L(H)=0 all hypotheses agree pointwise and zero regret is attainable. The domain T≥d avoids the separate saturation regime in which regret is capped by T.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a positive function g(d,T) and constants a,A>0 independent of both parameters, all label sets and all hypothesis classes, and prove a g(d,T)≤R(d,T)≤A g(d,T) for every integer T≥d≥1. Lower bounds may use families of classes; a worst-case class need not attain the supremum. This is an asymptotic regret target with multiplicative constants, not additive 0.01 error.

sentences: QAOA is a widely studied quantum optimization ansatz using alternating objective and mixing operations.
The SK model provides a canonical random quadratic objective with a known limiting optimum.
The question asks for the best limiting energy reachable by finite-depth QAOA when depth is subsequently allowed to grow.
Angles are optimized only after taking the infinite-size ensemble limit.
The source conjectures that this limiting value reaches the Parisi optimum, and the card now accepts a proved numerical determination within 0.01.

cards.definitions: For n≥2 let J_{ij}, 1≤i<j≤n, be independent real normal random variables of mean 0 and variance 1. On (ℂ²)^{⊗n}, let Z_i and X_i act on the i-th qubit by the Pauli matrices Z=diag(1,−1) and X with off-diagonal entries 1 and diagonal entries 0. Put H_J=n^{−1/2}Σ_{i<j}J_{ij}Z_iZ_j and B_n=Σ_i X_i. Let |+⟩=(|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2. For integer depth p≥1 and fixed real angle vectors γ,β∈ℝ^p, define |ψ_{p,J}⟩=e^{−iβ_p B_n}e^{−iγ_p H_J}⋯e^{−iβ₁ B_n}e^{−iγ₁ H_J}|+⟩^{⊗n}. Matrix exponentials have their usual convergent-series meaning; states have unit norm. Expectation is over J. The n limit exists for each fixed p and angles as established for this model in the source. Angles may depend on p but are fixed independently of n and J. First take the infinite-n ensemble limit for fixed angles, then optimize those angles, then take the supremum over finite depths. Supremum need not be attained. Identity layers imply that the optimized depth values are nondecreasing. They are bounded by Π*=lim_{n→∞} E_J[max_{z∈{−1,1}^n} n^{−1/2}Σ_{i<j}J_{ij}z_iz_j]/n, the finite Parisi ground-state value in this normalization. Maximization, rather than minimization, fixes the sign convention.
cards.answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous value a and a Lean proof that |a−A|≤1/100, or certified lower and upper bounds of width at most 1/50 with the midpoint as answer. Exact determination also qualifies. Merely restating the defining supremum, reporting floating-point optimization at finitely many depths, or interchanging depth and instance-size limits is insufficient. Equality with Π* is a stronger possible answer, not assumed by the target.

cards.definitions: Write [d]={1,…,d}, u_d(i)=1/d and d_TV(p,u_d)=(1/2)Σ_i|p_i−1/d|. The algorithm receives d and ε and oracle access to a unitary U_p satisfying U_p|0^k⟩=Σ_i√p_i|i⟩|ψ_i⟩, where each garbage state |ψ_i⟩ is normalized. The extension of U_p away from |0^k⟩ and its garbage states are arbitrary; the tester must work for every valid oracle satisfying the promise. A query is one application of U_p, U_p† or controlled-U_p; intervening quantum operations, ancillas and measurements are unrestricted and do not count toward query complexity. The code is used as a black box: the tester does not get a classical description to inspect for free. Let Q(d,ε) be the minimum worst-case number of such queries among testers whose probability of the correct yes/no output is at least 0.99 for every oracle with p=u_d or d_TV(p,u_d)>ε, taking the worst case over allowed oracle-register sizes. No guarantee is required in the intermediate gap.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a positive function g(d,ε) and absolute constants a,A>0 such that a g(d,ε)≤Q(d,ε)≤A g(d,ε) throughout the stated domain. Prove both bounds uniformly over its two parameters and all valid oracle implementations. A formula or certified evaluation rule may specify g; merely renaming Q is insufficient. This is an asymptotic query bound up to multiplicative constants, not pointwise additive 0.01 accuracy.

context_blocks.title: Running a sampler backwards is extra information
context_blocks.text: Ordinary sample access reveals only independent outcomes. Coherent access to a sampler and its inverse permits interference between executions. This can reduce the number of calls needed to detect a departure from uniformity; a classical sample lower bound therefore does not automatically apply.

context_blocks.title: The upper bound has two regimes
context_blocks.text: The paper establishes O(min{d^{1/3}/ε^{4/3},√d/ε}) queries. The terms cross at ε=d^{-1/2}: the first governs larger errors and the second smaller errors. The question asks whether any quantum tester can improve this full dependence.

context_blocks.title: Separate lower bounds leave a gap
context_blocks.text: The source recalls Ω(d^{1/3}) queries for constant ε and Ω(1/ε) already on a two-element domain. Knowing both separately does not yield their conjectured joint dependence. For example, at ε=d^{-1/2} the target is Ω(d).

context_blocks.title: A stronger variant fixes a special oracle structure
context_blocks.text: For a string x∈[d]^m, the standard oracle maps |j,z⟩ to |j,z⊕x_j⟩ and defines p_i=|{j:x_j=i}|/m. The authors also conjecture the same lower bound even with this structure available, in the worst case over m and x. This is a stronger claim than the arbitrary-synthesizer target selected here; fixed small m can cap the cost through reading the entire string.

context_blocks.title: Quantitative formulation
context_blocks.text: The original conjecture predicts Q(d,ε)=Θ(min{d^{1/3}ε^{−4/3},d^{1/2}ε^{−1}}), with its upper bound proved by the source. The retained target asks for the optimal joint function even if that candidate lower bound is false; it is not asserted to be logically equivalent to the conjecture.

The same tuple b must satisfy all 2^k−1 inequalities simultaneously.

sentences: Every tuple of strings has a profile of complexities of its nonempty subtuples.
The question asks whether that whole profile can be multiplied by any fixed positive real factor.
One new tuple must realize all the scaled quantities within logarithmic additive error.

cards.definitions: Fix one optimal plain Kolmogorov machine U: an optimal partial computable map from finite binary programs to finite binary strings. C(x) is the minimum program length with U(program)=x. For S={i₁<⋯<i_r}, encode the tuple x_S as 1^r0 followed, in that order, by the strings 1^{|x_i|}0x_i, and let C(x_S) mean the complexity of this encoding. This is a fixed computably decodable encoding. The strings b_i have no prescribed lengths and need not be computable from the a_i by a fixed transformation. Only joint unconditional complexities of all nonempty subtuples are required. The constants may depend on k, λ and U but not on n, the input strings or S. The additive slack is measured in bits. This uses the original length normalization O(log n); it does not silently replace it by the potentially smaller O(log C(a₁,…,a_k)).
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the displayed universal statement, or its logical negation with the same quantifier order. Failure of one algorithm for producing b, or failure of obtaining the scaling by conditioning the original strings on an auxiliary string, is not a refutation. The logarithmic slack is part of the proposition, not a numerical-estimation tolerance.

sentences: A halfspace is the sign of a weighted sum of input bits and a threshold.
Its degree-zero and degree-one Fourier coefficients measure its mean and coordinate correlations.
The question asks whether their squared weight is always at least 2/π.
Majority functions approach that proposed universal constant as dimension grows.
The exact inequality is retained because a general algorithm for merely approximating the extremal constant is already known.

cards.definitions: A linear threshold function has f(x)=sign(Σ_{i=1}^n w_ix_i−θ) for some real weights w_i and threshold θ, with sign(t)=1 when t≥0 and −1 otherwise. Constant functions are included. Under the uniform measure on {−1,1}^n, define f̂(S)=2^{−n}Σ_x f(x)∏_{i∈S}x_i, with empty product 1. Thus f̂(∅) is the mean and f̂({i}) is the correlation with the i-th coordinate. The displayed squared coefficients are the Fourier weight in degrees zero and one. There is no bound on dimension, weights or bias, and no regularity assumption on the halfspace. The constant π is the usual circle constant.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the exact universal inequality or give a threshold function with a rigorous proof that its low-degree weight is strictly less than 2/π. Approximation of the extremal constant to 0.01 would not settle this universal proposition. An algorithm for approximating that constant is already known; the retained target is the source’s sharp inequality.

sentences: Weighted k-server assigns a separate movement-cost multiplier to each server.
All distinct locations are at unit distance, isolating uncertainty about which weight to move.
The target is the optimal randomized competitive ratio as a function of the number of servers.
It takes the worst case over finite metric sizes and arbitrary positive weights against oblivious requests.
The recent exp(O(k²)) upper bound removes the old doubly-exponential barrier but leaves a substantial gap above exponential lower bounds.

cards.definitions: For k≥1 an instance environment consists of a finite set X with |X|≥k+1, uniform distance d(x,y)=1 if x≠y and 0 otherwise, positive real weights w₁,…,w_k, and an initial location c_i∈X for each labeled server i. Co-location is permitted. These data are known to the online algorithm. A finite request sequence σ∈X* is revealed one request at a time. Before proceeding, at least one server must occupy the requested location. Moving server i from x to y costs w_i d(x,y); all movements count. The algorithm may use arbitrary computation but cannot inspect future requests. OPT(σ) is the minimum cost of an offline execution with the same weights and initial locations. A real c≥1 is universally achievable for k if, for every environment, there are a randomized online strategy A and b≥0 such that for every finite σ, E[cost_A(σ)]≤c OPT(σ)+b. The strategy and b may depend on the environment; b may not depend on σ or its length. The sequence is fixed independently of the algorithm’s private random choices, and expectation is over those choices. Define R_w(k) as the infimum of universally achievable c. It is finite by known upper bounds and need not be attained. Metric size and the ratios between server weights are unbounded independently of k. No running-time bound or bit encoding of the real weights is imposed; the target measures online movement cost.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a positive function g(k) and constants a,A>0,k₀ such that a g(k)≤R_w(k)≤A g(k) for every integer k≥k₀, proving both bounds in the specified randomized model. Constants must not depend on metric size or weights. An improvement for one algorithm, fixed weight ratios or a bounded number of locations does not by itself determine this worst-case function. Precision is multiplicative constant factors in R_w, not additive 0.01 and not merely constant factors in its logarithm.

importance.reason: Downward self-reducibility of integer factoring asks whether a canonical arithmetic search problem has the recursive structure common to complete problems.
importance.basis: Individual scientific-importance reconsideration of the previous 500-card removal proposal; no category quotas or score threshold used.

sentences: Factoring is a central arithmetic search problem whose complete output is a unique prime-power decomposition.
The question asks whether one can factor an n-bit number in polynomial time given oracle answers only on shorter numbers.
All queries must have fewer than n bits, not merely a smaller numerical value.
The reducer is deterministic and uniform, with polynomially many ordinary computation steps.
A positive answer would place factoring in a more structured total-search class and reveal a basic recursive property of the problem.

cards.definitions: The input is the ordinary base-two expansion of N without leading zeroes, and n=⌊log₂N⌋+1. The output is the list of distinct increasing primes q₁<⋯<q_r and positive integer exponents e_i, all in binary, with N=∏_i q_i^{e_i}. A prime input has the single pair (N,1). The oracle returns the same unique prime-factorization representation on M. Queries may be adaptive but must all satisfy ⌊log₂M⌋+1<n relative to the original input length. Merely requiring M<N would be weaker and is not the target. The ordinary Turing-machine cost includes writing queries, reading answers and writing the output; supplying a correct oracle answer is the sole oracle operation. The output length of prime factorization is polynomial in n. There is no randomness, advice or nonuniform family of reducers. The reduction must work for every input, with one polynomial bound independent of its factorization.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove existence of the uniform polynomial-time reduction or its logical negation. Factoring using smaller numerical values of the same bit length, arbitrary smaller circuits for a factoring relation, or an exponential-time recursion does not meet the stated definition. The output need not be a decimal expansion of the input; its prime-power representation is explicit.

methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.

benchmark_selection.basis: Individual editorial review of saved titles, importance rationales, problem statements, source notes and working summaries. This is a review of importance and topical diversity, not a fresh verification of open status or completion of draft formulations. Importance scores are preserved.
